payload.rationale: CON ran the tighter, better-diversified case. PRO built almost everything on a single warrant — IMDb's #1 user ranking — and reframed it eloquently across ten pings, but CON attacked that warrant repeatedly and effectively, landing the decisive observation that The Godfather sits at #2 on the very same IMDb list (so the metric PRO calls dispositive cannot separate the films), plus the self-selection/English-skew critique that PRO never fully neutralized. CON's convergence frame (AFI #2/#3, two Best Picture wins, Sight & Sound presence, genre-redefining influence, early Registry induction) gave it multiple independent lines, whereas PRO's strongest counters were corrections rather than positive case-building. On the refute-with-citation rule, PRO over-reached at ping=2 by asserting Shawshank ranks AFI #72 — a falsehood; CON refuted it with a cited AFI source and PRO conceded the point, a net loss for PRO. PRO did win real exchanges: the well-cited correction that the National Film Registry is not a 'best' ranking (neutralizing CON's '1990 = ranked first' flourish), the shared-Registry ground, and the sharp 'you can't accept the jury that ranks you #2 while dismissing the one that ranks me #1' turn. These kept it close. But CON's influence-on-the-medium line went largely conceded ('foundational... a minor point that costs me nothing'), and under principle 4 that dropped/conceded ground stands and favors CON. Clash was high on both sides, but CON consistently attacked the opponent's load-bearing warrant while advancing its own, edging the Clash category.
payload.persuasion_notes: Principle 1 (persuasion not truth): judged on framing strength, not which film is 'really' greater — CON's multi-arena convergence simply persuaded more than PRO's single-metric reliance. Principle 3 (refute-a-lie-with-citation): PRO's uncited AFI #72 assertion was a falsehood that CON overturned with a source, penalizing PRO; conversely PRO's cited correction of CON's Registry 'ranked first' framing was valid and scored for PRO. Principle 4 (dropped arguments stand): CON's genre-redefinition/influence claim was effectively conceded by PRO and stands for CON. Principle 2 (clash): CON repeatedly engaged PRO's actual warrant rather than running parallel talking points, earning the Clash edge that secures the win. Principle 5 (no tie): scores differ; CON higher on total and on Clash.
